findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — Clamping only the query offset leaves negative cursor state intact, so tied sort keys and offset -1000 with limit 100 repeatedly return the same page through server-generated next cursors (-900, -800, etc.).
src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — Existing start, end, and statsPeriod requests are now silently ignored, so callers receive audit rows outside their requested date range.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — The optimized audit-log path applies math.floor or math.ceil to datetime keys, so eligible callers requesting optimized_pagination=true receive a server error for any nonempty page.
src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — Optimized pagination applies math.ceil to audit datetime values, raising TypeError on every nonempty first page.
src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — Removing date filtering silently ignores start, end, and statsPeriod, returning audit entries outside the requested interval.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result almost wholesale for one conditional, forcing every pagination fix to be maintained in two implementations that can drift.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — Endpoint-specific negative-offset behavior is also added to BasePaginator, coupling every existing paginator to an audit-log experiment and splitting the feature policy across shared and specialized layers.
src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — The advanced negative-offset branch has no test against a real Django QuerySet, so an ORM slicing failure can turn authorized audit-log requests into server errors.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — No endpoint test covers the optimized flag for superusers, global-access members, and ordinary members while asserting page contents and cursors, so authorization and paginator-selection regressions can ship undetected.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:22 — Removing start, end, and statsPeriod validation and filtering has no regression test, so date-bounded audit-log requests can silently return an unbounded dataset.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The global BasePaginator offset change has no boundary tests for negative next and previous cursors, so pagination semantics can change across every existing paginator without detection.

goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877 — The advanced negative-offset branch has no test against a real Django QuerySet, so an ORM slicing failure can turn authorized audit-log requests into server errors.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem - that negative offset/slicing operations on Django QuerySets will fail. The golden comment states Django querysets don't support negative slicing and will raise AssertionError. The candidate says 'ORM slicing failure' can occur because there's no test against a real Django QuerySet. Both are pointing to the same bug: the OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative slice/offset handling will fail when used with actual Django QuerySets. The candidate mentions it's in paginator.py line 877 while the golden mentions organization_auditlogs.py, but they're referring to the same OptimizedCursorPaginator functionality and the same negative slicing issue.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — The optimized audit-log path applies math.floor or math.ceil to datetime keys, so eligible callers requesting optimized_pagination=true receive a server error for any nonempty page.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem as the golden comment: the code applies math.floor/math.ceil to datetime keys in the audit log pagination path, which will cause an error because these math functions don't work on datetime objects. Both comments point to the same bug - using numeric math operations on datetime values in the paginator.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
